events.title: Titus Becomes Roman Emperor
events.description: After the death of his father Vespasian the previous day, Titus succeeded him as emperor of Rome. His short reign saw the opening of the Colosseum and the eruption of Mount Vesuvius.
events.significance: Titus's accession continued the Flavian dynasty, and a smooth succession from father to son kept the empire stable.

events.title: Henry VIII Crowned King of England
events.description: Henry VIII was crowned at Westminster Abbey. He was not yet 18 years old.
events.significance: His reign led to the English Reformation, the break with Rome, and major changes to English government and religion.

events.title: Manila Founded
events.description: The Spanish conquistador Miguel López de Legazpi founded Manila as a Spanish colonial capital in the Philippines.
events.significance: Manila became a hub of the Pacific trade between Asia and the Americas and has remained the center of Philippine political life.

events.title: Napoleon's Invasion of Russia Begins
events.description: Napoleon's Grande Armée crossed the Neman River into Russian territory with several hundred thousand troops.
events.significance: The campaign ended in catastrophic losses for France and began the decline of Napoleon's power in Europe.

events.title: France and Italy Sign an Armistice
events.description: Two days after France signed an armistice with Germany, it signed a separate one with Italy near Rome. The agreement was to take effect once both armistices were in force.
events.significance: It marked the formal end of France's fighting in the Second World War's western campaign and left the country divided under occupation and the Vichy regime.
